findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify in AC5 (or the Testing section) how many attempts are acceptable and/or what input characteristics guarantee the move fires reliably (e.g. 'use epic 061c story S1 as the test ticket, which is known-bad; retry up to N times or until emitted').
evidence: "a REAL rebar review-plan run emits the move, with the output attached to this ticket as a comment (not a unit-test-only demonstration)"

"Contrast: a review of a ticket with a symbol-derived inventory does not emit it (recorded, not asserted in a unit test — LLM output is not deterministic enough to gate CI on)" — non-determinism is acknowledged only for AC7, not AC5
findings.finding: AC5 asserts that a real `rebar review-plan` run 'emits the move' as a hard pass/fail criterion, but LLM output is non-deterministic. The plan acknowledges non-determinism only for the contrast case (AC7). If the move does not fire on the first attempt (e.g. the prompt did not trigger the criterion), the executor has no guidance on how to proceed — retry with a different ticket? Adjust the input? Declare success anyway?
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC5; Testing section — 'Real run'
scenarios: Executor runs rebar review-plan against a hand-enumerated ticket and the move is not emitted on the first run; no guidance on how many retries are acceptable or what alternate input to use.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend AC5 to: 'a REAL `rebar review-plan` run against epic 061c / S1 (whose inventory is known hand-enumerated) emits the move; retry up to 3 runs if the first does not fire (LLM non-determinism); attach the first successful output as a ticket comment.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify in AC7 where the contrast-case result must be recorded (e.g. 'attached as a comment on this ticket alongside the AC5 output' or 'in a `docs/` log file committed with the PR').

findings.finding: AC7 ('the contrast case is recorded') does not specify WHERE or in WHAT FORM the recording must appear. 'Recorded' is not tied to a repo artifact, ticket comment, or other verifiable location, making the AC unverifiable by an independent reviewer.
scenarios: Reviewer cannot determine whether AC7 is satisfied because 'recorded' could mean a comment on the ticket, a file in the repo, a note in the PR description, or nothing at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend AC7 to: 'the contrast case is recorded as a comment on this ticket: a review of [named ticket with symbol-derived inventory] did not emit the move (screenshot or CLI output excerpt attached).'

A future contributor adding a new project criterion could repeat the mistake of wiring it to code_review.
findings.location: Approach section (ground truth item 2) and AC line 3-4
scenarios: A future engineer adds a new project.* criterion and tries to also add a code_review move for it, wasting time debugging why the move never fires.

findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-paragraph entry to `.rebar/AGENTS.md` (or equivalent) under a 'Criterion routing constraints' section: 'Code-review coaching moves use a closed applies_when vocabulary (OVERLAY_IDS ∪ always). Project-scoped criterion ids (project.*) are not in this set and will never trigger a code-review move; route them to plan_review only. See code_review/moves.py:1-9 and code_review/workflow_ops.py::code_review_coach_inputs for the gate logic.' Reference this note from the Scope section of the plan.

findings.finding: The plan claims to 'Follow the existing `project.portability` pattern exactly, which is three files,' but the real pattern ships four committed assets plus a contract-tested docs subsection. The missing assets are: (a) `.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-portability.eval.yaml` — an 8-case calibration corpus; and (b) the `### Dogfooding a project portability guard` subsection in `docs/plan-review-gate.md`, whose presence is enforced by `tests/unit/test_project_portability_docs.py`. Shipping a partial copy of a named pattern without rationale for the omissions is a cargo-cult copy — the executor follows the three-file scope literally and the criterion ships without a calibration baseline.
findings.location: Approach section ('Follow the existing `project.portability` pattern exactly, which is three files') and Scope section (lists only three files)
scenarios: Executor follows the three-file scope literally; criterion ships without a calibration corpus; the only quality gate is the single non-repeatable live-run comment, meaning precision/recall are permanently uncharacterized.

A future `rebar criteria eval project.symbol-reference-completeness --runs 3` invocation has no corpus to run against, making the calibration step from the `project.portability` pattern impossible to replicate.

findings.finding: `.gitignore` uses surgical `!` un-ignore lines for every committed `.rebar/` file (e.g. `!.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-portability.md`, `!.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-portability.eval.yaml`). findings.finding: The criterion prompt file (`plan-review-project-symbol-reference-completeness.md`) is specified only as 'detect a plan whose affected-file / call-site inventory was enumerated by hand (or is demonstrably incomplete) rather than derived from the symbol graph' — but the detection protocol, emission threshold, and required finding fields are never defined. The plan claims to 'follow the existing `project.portability` pattern exactly,' yet that pattern specifies a 4-element counterexample requirement (cited plan mechanism + alternate shape + causal failure mechanism + observable breakage), a complete list of required finding fields with types, explicit non-finding guidance, and a named support matrix. None of the analogous elements — what evidence constitutes 'hand-enumerated' (vs. incomplete but tool-derived), what threshold governs emission, what fields the LLM must populate — are defined for this criterion.
scenarios: The executor writes a prompt that fires on plans with 10 named files ('10 files looks like it might be hand-enumerated') with no falsifiable criterion, producing noisy advisory findings on every non-trivial scope section

findings.suggested_fix: Mirror the `plan-review-project-portability.md` structure: add (1) a Finding threshold section requiring the reviewer to demonstrate a SPECIFIC symbol/file that the plan names by hand and that a `find_referencing_symbols` query would have surfaced but did not; (2) a Required finding fields section listing `location: str`, `finding: str`, `evidence: list[str]`, `criteria: list[str]` with the same field-contract prose; and (3) a Non-findings section stating that a plan which cites Serena tools in its scope section, or whose scope was demonstrably generated by a symbol query, is not a finding.

findings.finding: The plan says 'Follow the existing `project.portability` pattern exactly' but scopes only three files, while the `project.portability` pattern actually ships four committed assets: criteria_routing.json entry, prompt file, plan_review_moves.json entry, AND an eval corpus (`.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-portability.eval.yaml`). The plan also omits a docs subsection (analogous to the `project.portability` dogfood example in `docs/plan-review-gate.md`, which is contract-tested by `test_project_portability_docs.py`). Claiming 'exactly' while silently omitting two of four pattern assets is a cargo-cult partial copy — the executor may not realise the pattern includes an eval corpus and docs entry, and the Testing section provides no calibration corpus for the new criterion.
findings.location: Scope section / Approach ('Follow the existing `project.portability` pattern exactly, which is three files')
